memory_update.text: HealthStream is the cleanest small-cap underfollowed candidate for the credentialing_assessment_and_proctoring node because its product suite directly covers healthcare credentialing, privileging, provider enrollment, performance assessment, and compliance learning.

Graham Holdings should remain in the underfollowed lane as a hidden Kaplan exposure: professional licensure, certification prep, and continuing education are housed inside a diversified holding company rather than a pure-play education ticker.

Adtalem is a second-order regulated workforce-output beneficiary rather than a direct assessment infrastructure company; require licensure pass-rate, accreditation, and clinical-capacity evidence before upgrading.

Prometric, ProctorU/Meazure, UWorld, Colibri/Becker, Respondus, Honorlock, Proctorio, Kryterion, and many professional associations appear important to the node but are not clean US-listed public equities; track them as private/customer/supplier context rather than candidates.

node: Credentialing, assessment, licensure-prep, and proctoring infrastructure
summary: Layer 1B expands the credentialing/assessment/proctoring node with a two-lane universe. Pearson is the reference anchor for high-stakes testing infrastructure. The underfollowed discovery lane is stronger in healthcare credentialing workflow software and professional licensure/CE prep than in generic course delivery. Best-fit small/mid-cap discovery names are HealthStream for healthcare credentialing and provider-compliance infrastructure, Graham Holdings via Kaplan for exam prep/licensure/CE, and Adtalem as a healthcare workforce/licensure-output beneficiary rather than pure testing infrastructure.
